prompt: Held–Karp solves TSP by storing the best path for each visited subset and last city. What does this gain over enumerating every tour?

options.text: A polynomial-time exact algorithm for all TSP inputs
options.explanation: There are still exponentially many subsets.

options.text: Reuse of shared subproblems, with an exponential subset cost remaining
options.explanation: It avoids recomputing many common prefixes but does not remove exponential growth.

options.text: A faster answer that may violate tour constraints
options.explanation: Held–Karp remains exact; approximation is a different strategy.

options.text: A measured runtime determined solely by the city count
options.explanation: Asymptotic bounds leave constants, implementation and hardware unspecified.

workedExample: Many tour prefixes visit the same subset and end in the same city. Keeping only the cheapest such prefix lets Held–Karp reuse work instead of trying every full ordering. There are still exponentially many subsets. The improvement changes the growth substantially but does not give a polynomial-time exact algorithm.
